title: Autism Regulatory Variant Atlas — Replication Ledger
description: Every major claim this project tested, with where it was first seen, where it was retested, whether it held, and its current evidence tier. Records failures and corrections as first-class entries. Literature anchors (published findings not tested here) are labeled sourceType='literature-anchor'.

tier_key.A: Tested against an appropriate null and survived. Citable.
tier_key.A-minus: Survives a targeted test but with caveats (borderline p, limited scope, gene-set-sensitive).
tier_key.B: Statistically real but not specific to the gene set under study.
tier_key.C: Descriptive or structural. No statistical claim.
tier_key.D: Was presented as significant, later corrected, withdrawn, or falsified.
tier_key.E: Partial or proxy test, underpowered. Not support, not falsification.
tier_key.established: Published literature anchor, not tested by this project.

status_key.replicated: Held up under a null test.
status_key.replicated-scoped: Real, but confined to a specific gene or context; does not generalize.
status_key.not-gene-set-specific: Real signal, but other gene sets produce it equally.
status_key.failed-to-replicate: Did not reproduce in an independent dataset.
status_key.partially-failed: Some component held, the headline framing did not.
status_key.corrected: Initially significant, later shown wrong or artifactual.
status_key.inconclusive: Test run but underpowered or a proxy; verdict open.

entries.claim: Gene pairs with a direct regulatory edge are more co-disrupted in ASD brain than other NDD gene pairs.

firstObserved.statistic: cross-reg pairs rho=0.158 vs non-cross-reg NDD 0.082

replicationTests.statistic: MWU p=0.006, permutation p=0.021

entries.takeaway: The strongest surviving finding. Specific regulatory wiring, not just NDD membership, predicts co-disruption.

entries.claim: Individual regulatory edges between NDD transcription factors and ion-channel genes are stronger than both random genes and other NDD genes for the same targets.

firstObserved.statistic: 5/10 edges supported, mean 77.5th pctl vs null 25-26th

replicationTests.statistic: n_sig p=0.82, median|Z| p=0.60 — confound ruled out

entries.takeaway: Tests individual edge strength, NOT network-level convergence. The wiring between specific gene pairs is real and specific; a coordinated cascade is a separate, unproven claim.
entries.nullTest: Random knockdowns and NDD comparators; expression-matched.

entries.claim: The FOXP2/HDAC4 regulatory module carries excess de novo variants in autism.

replicationTests.statistic: p=0.0001, leave-one-out robust, 0 in controls

entries.takeaway: Independent of the GPF signal that later collapsed (uses denovo-db).

entries.claim: A TCF4 enhancer variant is supported as regulatory by multiple independent methods.

firstObserved.dataset: multi-tool (Hi-C, FLARE, ENCODE4 rE2G, Evo2, BRAIN-MAGNET, AlphaGenome)

replicationTests.statistic: 6/6 concordant

entries.takeaway: Convergent orthogonal support; the single best-validated regulatory element in the project.

entries.claim: MEF2C haploinsufficiency preferentially dysregulates other NDD transcription factors in patient organoids.

firstObserved.statistic: 6/16 network genes vs 4/107 non-network, Fisher p=0.0003, permutation p=0.0002

replicationTests.system: specificity test — does it generalize to other perturbations?
replicationTests.statistic: MEF2C-specific; knocking out FOXP1/MYT1L/BCL11A/MECP2 does NOT reproduce the cross-regulation

entries.takeaway: Real and properly nulled, but it is MEF2C-specific — a topological property of where MEF2C sits, not a general cascade among the genes.
entries.nullTest: Permutation over full NDD gene pool; cross-perturbation generalization test.

entries.claim: Predicted downstream effects match observed direction in CHOOSE inhibitory-lineage neurons.

replicationTests.system: sign test across all cell types
replicationTests.statistic: overall 13/27 p=0.72; excitatory shows opposite direction

entries.takeaway: Signal is real only in the inhibitory lineage; the excitatory lineage points the other way, so the overall prediction does not hold.
entries.nullTest: Sign test across all cell types.

entries.claim: The core gene set is enriched for common ASD GWAS signal.

replicationTests.statistic: weakens to p=0.061; 5-gene swap flips significance

entries.takeaway: Gene-set-sensitive — the result flips depending on which genes are included. Classic fragility.
entries.nullTest: 100K permutations vs null NDD gene sets.

entries.claim: The core genes are unusually developmentally co-expressed in fetal brain.

replicationTests.dataset: 10K permutations of high-pLI brain genes + BH correction
replicationTests.statistic: p=0.018, fragile under BH across 8 findings; subset selection unclear

entries.takeaway: Borderline and fragile; the 5-gene subset selection may be post-hoc. Demoted A→A- in the April 2026 audit.

entries.claim: Multiple autism-gene knockouts converge on the same specific downstream bottleneck genes (KCNIP4, DLGAP1, GRIK1, etc.).

firstObserved.statistic: 65 genes hit by 5+ perturbations, 9/65 neuro-signaling, OR=9.36 p<0.0001; glutamate receptors OR=45.7

replicationTests.statistic: OR=1.01, p=0.52 — zero of 10 key genes reached significance
all controlled p>0.64 — no specificity vs other neuronal genes

entries.takeaway: The convergence PHENOMENON is real in all three datasets, but the SPECIFIC genes that converge differ every time. There is no universal bottleneck gene list. This is the project's central negative result.
entries.nullTest: Controlled comparison vs other neuronal genes; independent datasets.

entries.claim: Ion-channel disruption is a common downstream endpoint across many autism/NDD gene knockouts.

replicationTests.statistic: KCNA2 hit by 7/9 mutations at Day 25; multiple Ca/Na channels early
not specific to any particular upstream gene set

entries.takeaway: Robust and replicated as a convergence endpoint, but it happens for essentially any NDD gene knockout — it does not single out a special upstream network.
entries.nullTest: Comparison against other upstream gene sets.

entries.claim: MECP2 is a common downstream casualty of diverse upstream autism mutations.

firstObserved.statistic: 5/9 mutations disrupt MECP2 at Day 25, mostly down

replicationTests.statistic: real cross-mutation signal, but not specific to any particular gene set

entries.takeaway: MECP2 goes down regardless of which upstream gene is hit — a convergent casualty, not evidence for a specific cascade.

entries.claim: GABA receptors drive epilepsy and glutamate receptors drive autism, as receptor classes.

firstObserved.statistic: glutamate convergent in autism, GABA burdened in epilepsy, apparent zero overlap

replicationTests.statistic: epilepsy MWU p=0.189
GRIN2A (glutamate) significant epilepsy burden p=0.009 — breaks glutamate=autism

entries.takeaway: The class-level separation did not hold. What survives is a small set of specific shared genes (SCN2A, KCNB1, PCDH19, GRIN2A) that span both conditions. Reframed accordingly.
entries.nullTest: Class membership predicting condition; individual-gene falsifier.

entries.claim: The core network genes are disrupted together in ASD postmortem brain.

firstObserved.statistic: network genes disrupted, p=0.032 vs random

replicationTests.statistic: other NDD TF sets show equal/greater convergence with the same ion-channel targets

entries.takeaway: Real disruption, but nothing distinguishes this network from other NDD gene sets. 'Consistent with,' not 'validates.'
entries.nullTest: Comparison against other NDD transcription-factor sets.

entries.claim: The core network is preferentially disrupted in dup15q organoids.

replicationTests.statistic: network at 52nd percentile — not preferentially disrupted

entries.takeaway: Direction concordance is real but the network is not preferentially hit; it sits at chance for breadth.

entries.claim: Population-level regulatory-variant enrichment validates the core network (3.4x, p=0.00055).

replicationTests.statistic: 0/9 families survive; driven by an HDAC4 + chromatin-loop artifact

entries.takeaway: Collapsed entirely on rescoring. An artifact, not a signal. One of the project's key confirmation-bias corrections.

entries.claim: CUX1 is a master regulator driving the autism cell-type program.

replicationTests.statistic: targets 17.8% of ALL genes; LDSC p=0.31 — not a specific autism regulator

entries.takeaway: The 64% figure reflects CUX1's enormous target breadth, not autism specificity. Its breadth could still be mechanistically relevant, but the 'master autism regulator' claim is falsified.

entries.claim: MEF2C regulates roughly half of all autism genes (a uniquely powerful hub).

replicationTests.statistic: #259/644 TFs (1.30x); 4 other TFs cover more

entries.takeaway: MEF2C is unremarkable by raw target count. Its importance is topological (where it sits), not quantitative — a distinction the project now keeps strict.

entries.claim: The proband carries pathogenic coding variants in MEF2C / DYRK1A / EP300.

replicationTests.statistic: MEF2C 'frameshifts' both intronic (one AF 42%); DYRK1A variant homozygous in father; EP300 deletion part of a common haplotype

entries.takeaway: All were common or benign. Reinforces the project's starting point: the proband's exome is negative, and inherited/common variation is where the model lives.

entries.claim: Seven shared transcription factors regulate all five core genes.

replicationTests.statistic: only 1 (TBX20) shows the expected brain pattern; 4/7 not expressed

entries.takeaway: Most of the 'shared regulators' are not expressed in brain. Computational inference without an expression filter.

entries.claim: Cross-regulatory wiring creates compounding (amplifying) vulnerability across the network.

replicationTests.statistic: p=0.31; ~33% power at d=0.5; CHOOSE 86% zeros (uninformative); right experiment not done

entries.takeaway: Tested three times, never demonstrated — but the data are too underpowered to call it falsified. The proper experiment (multi-gene partial knockdown in a sensitized background) has not been run.

entries.claim: The core genes are uniquely co-regulated by shared upstream factors.

replicationTests.statistic: p=0.24; positive trend, not significant; proxy tests 'more shared TFs' not 'coordinated regulation'

entries.takeaway: A positive trend that never reaches significance, using a proxy for the real question. Not support, not falsification.
entries.nullTest: Permutation vs random SFARI sets (power undocumented).

entries.claim: The core regulatory programs carry common-variant ASD heritability.

replicationTests.statistic: TCF4 p=0.84, MEF2C p=0.93, EP300 p=0.29 — all null, but LDSC underpowered for small gene-set annotations

entries.takeaway: All null, but LDSC needs thousands of SNPs to have power; small gene-set annotations can't be tested this way. A method-power limit, not demonstrated absence.
entries.nullTest: LDSC (known low power at this scale).

entries.claim: Common regulatory-variant burden at NDD genes is correlated/structured in the population (and elevated in the proband).

replicationTests.statistic: burden segregates independently (obs/exp 1.0-1.6x); pathway rho ~0.01; proband 0/10 genes in bottom 5%

entries.takeaway: Negative in this specific design, but the design had no ASD cases, used monogenic (not GWAS) genes, adult brain models, and a tiny sample. Does NOT weigh against common noncoding variants in autism — see literature anchors below.

entries.claim: Molecular disruption magnitude tracks clinical autism severity.

replicationTests.statistic: all p>0.10

entries.takeaway: A clean, publishable negative: molecular disruption magnitude does not predict severity across any of 16 metrics tested.

entries.claim: Common inherited variation accounts for the majority of autism heritability (~52% of liability).

firstObserved.statistic: narrow-sense h2 ~52%; common inherited ~49% of variance; rare de novo ~2.6%

replicationTests.statistic: established

entries.takeaway: The anchor for why the project studies inherited/common variation. Rare de novo variants have large individual effect but small population contribution; common inherited variation carries the bulk of heritability.

entries.claim: All genome-wide-significant ASD GWAS loci are noncoding/regulatory.

firstObserved.dataset: Grove et al. 2019, Nature Genetics (18,381 ASD cases)
firstObserved.statistic: 5 genome-wide-significant loci, all noncoding; SNP-h2 explains ~12% of liability so far

replicationTests.statistic: established; implicated genes (KCNN2, KMT2E, PTBP2, MACROD2) do not overlap the monogenic NDD set

entries.takeaway: Supports a regulatory/noncoding architecture for common ASD risk, and shows the common-variant genes differ from the monogenic NDD genes the project's own tests focused on.

entries.claim: Most monogenic NDD genes are eQTL-free in developing brain, but a subset carries prenatal-specific, expression-reducing regulatory variation.

firstObserved.statistic: 27/39 NDD genes zero eQTLs; 12 have prenatal-specific/trending, expression-reducing eQTLs (e.g. MECP2 prenatal p=6.25e-5 beta=-0.371; EP300 p=8.87e-7 beta=-0.41)

replicationTests.statistic: prenatal effects invisible in adult GTEx

entries.takeaway: Marks the 12 genes where rare (monogenic) and common (regulatory) mechanisms both plausibly operate, and shows adult-brain models (like the project's ChromBPNet test) miss prenatal effects.
